implementation_notes: TypeORM realizes the composite with decorators: the root declares @OneToMany relations, cascade: true makes the related objects inserted and updated with the root, onDelete: CASCADE lets the database delete dependents, and orphanedRowAction: 'delete' removes children a cascade save no longer finds. The documentation warns explicitly that cascades are a less explicit way of saving and can persist unintended objects, so the cascade boundary should be as narrow as the aggregate.
pitfalls: cascade: true on a wide relation is a data-loss and security hazard: whatever object is attached gets persisted, and cascade remove only traverses relations that are actually loaded.
orphanedRowAction defaults to nullify, but a non-nullable foreign key makes the orphan row be deleted instead - a difference that only shows in the schema.
Cascade remove needs the relation eager- or explicitly loaded, otherwise a remove leaves the children in place.

variants.name: Prisma nested writes (create / connect / delete in one call)
variants.implementation_notes: Prisma expresses the unit declaratively in the schema and in a single nested write: the contract declares the relation fields, and one client call creates the parent together with its children (filling in foreign keys), connects existing children or disconnects them, so the cluster is written as one statement tree. There is no identity map: use include on reads and the nested-write call on writes, and model upserts explicitly because connectOrCreate-style helpers are not available.
pitfalls: disconnect leaves the child row in place with a null foreign key; only delete/deleteMany removes it, so clusters accumulate silent orphans.
Nested writes are a relational-database feature: on MongoDB the same operation must be split into two writes with the reference set by hand.
A large nested write is one interactive transaction, holding locks longer than an equivalent batch insert.
